definition: MTU defines the largest packet size that can be transmitted over a network link without fragmentation. Misconfigured MTU settings can cause performance issues or be exploited in certain fragmentation-based attacks.
examContext: SY0-701 may reference MTU in the context of network performance troubleshooting or packet fragmentation attacks that attempt to evade inspection by security devices.

detail.practicalScenario: Chen troubleshoots intermittent VPN connection drops and discovers the tunnel's MTU setting is too large for the path, causing packets to be silently dropped rather than fragmented. Lowering the MTU on the VPN interface resolves the connectivity issue immediately.
detail.quizQuestion: Users report intermittent connectivity issues over a VPN tunnel, and the root cause is traced to oversized packets being silently dropped along the path. Which setting should be adjusted?

definition: NAC enforces security policy by evaluating a device's compliance, such as updated antivirus or patches, before granting it access to the network, and can restrict or quarantine non-compliant devices. It's commonly used to secure both wired and wireless connections against unauthorized or unhealthy devices.
examContext: SY0-701 ties NAC to posture assessment before granting network access, often placing non-compliant devices into a quarantine VLAN for remediation before full access is granted.

detail.practicalScenario: Maria deploys NAC so that any device connecting to the corporate network is first checked for up-to-date antivirus signatures and OS patches. A visitor's laptop missing critical patches is automatically placed into a quarantine VLAN with only internet access until it is remediated.
detail.quizQuestion: A visitor's laptop connects to the corporate network but is automatically restricted to a quarantine VLAN because it is missing critical security patches. Which technology enforced this policy?

definition: NAT translates private internal IP addresses to a public IP address, and vice versa, as traffic crosses a network boundary, allowing multiple internal devices to share a single public address. It also provides a degree of security by hiding internal network addressing from external view.
examContext: SY0-701 ties NAT to both IP address conservation and a basic obscurity benefit; know NAT is not a substitute for a firewall, since it doesn't inherently filter traffic based on security policy.

detail.practicalScenario: Sam's office has only one public IP address from its ISP but dozens of internal workstations needing internet access. He configures NAT on the edge router so all internal devices share the single public address for outbound connections, while their actual private addresses stay hidden from the internet.
detail.quizQuestion: An office has only one public IP address but needs dozens of internal workstations to access the internet simultaneously. Which technology makes this possible?

items.name: Static NAT
items.detail: One-to-one fixed mapping between a private and a public address. Used to publish an internal server.

items.name: Dynamic NAT
items.detail: Private addresses are mapped to a pool of public addresses on demand.

items.name: PAT (NAT overload)
items.detail: Many private hosts share ONE public IP, distinguished by port numbers. What home routers do.

items.name: DNAT / port forwarding
items.detail: Destination NAT: rewrites the destination of inbound traffic so an outside client can reach an internal service.

items.name: Security note
items.detail: NAT hides internal addressing but is NOT a firewall; it provides no real protection by itself.

definition: An NDA is a legal contract that obligates the signing parties to keep specified information confidential and not disclose it to unauthorized third parties. It's commonly signed by employees, contractors, and business partners who will have access to sensitive data.
examContext: SY0-701 groups NDA with other agreement types like MOU and BPA; know an NDA specifically protects confidentiality of information rather than defining service terms or performance expectations.

detail.practicalScenario: Jordan has every contractor sign an NDA before granting them access to the company's proprietary source code repository. When a former contractor later tries to share internal code snippets publicly, the signed NDA gives legal grounds to pursue action against the disclosure.
detail.quizQuestion: Before granting a contractor access to proprietary source code, a company requires them to sign a document legally obligating them to keep that information confidential. What is this document called?
